# SOC 2 Readiness Review - September

**Date:** 2026-09-10 · **Attendees:** Sam Whitfield, Maya Chen, Marcus Bell, Hana Ito · **Status column updated:** 2026-10-09

## Purpose

Halfway point check on the Type II observation window (2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31). I walked every recurring control in SOC 2 Program Overview and asked: if Ledgerwise Assurance sampled this today, would we have the evidence?

## Summary

Most controls are healthy. Three gaps would produce Type II exceptions if they're not closed and documented.

| # | Gap | Severity | Owner | Due | Status (Oct 9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Q3 quarterly access review not done | High | Sam | 2026-10-10 | 70% (14 of 20 systems) |
| 2 | Vendor risk assessments missing for DriveWealth, Lithic, Alloy, Customer.io | Medium | Sam | 2026-10-24 | 2 of 4 done |
| 3 | MDM on 88% of laptops (60 of 68); control requires 100% | Medium | Sam | 2026-10-17 | 96% (65 of 68) |

## Gap 1: access reviews

The Access Review Procedure requires a quarterly review of every in-scope system, completed by quarter end. Q2 was done in July after I joined. Q3 had not started on Sep 10, mostly because I spent August on policies and the system owners were deep in the ACH cut-over and investing beta.

Plan: run the review Sep 21 to Sep 30 with system owners signing in the Q3 Access Review Tracker.

Update (Oct 9): we missed Sep 30. 14 of 20 systems signed off. The remaining six are lower-risk tools, owners have been chased, and I expect to close on Oct 10. A late completion will be documented as an exception with root cause (launch load on owners) and the Q4 review will start Dec 1 rather than mid-December.

## Gap 2: vendor risk assessments

The Vendor Risk Register lists every critical vendor, but four have never had a formal assessment against our questionnaire: DriveWealth (live since beta), Lithic (signed, not live), Alloy (KYC since June), Customer.io (marketing notifications).

Update (Oct 9): Vendor Risk Assessment - DriveWealth done 2026-09-24; Vendor Risk Assessment - Lithic done 2026-10-02. Alloy is waiting on their current SOC 2 bridge letter. Customer.io questionnaire is with their team.

## Gap 3: MDM

68 laptops (64 employees, 4 contractors). On Sep 10, 60 enrolled. The 8 missing were a mix of contractor machines, two Linux workstations and people who ignored the enrollment email.

Update (Oct 9): 65 of 68. Remaining: two Linux engineering workstations (agent rollout in progress) and one laptop belonging to someone on leave until Oct 14. Plan in MDM Rollout Plan.

## What's healthy

- Change management: two-approval check on money-movement paths working since July (Type I observation 1 closed).
- Offboarding: 9 departures/contract ends since July, all deprovisioned within 1 business day.
- Training: 100% of staff completed annual security training.
- Backup restore test: Q3 restore done Aug 27.
- Incident handling: April 6 and Sep 26 both have complete write-ups (Incident Review Process).

## Decisions

Decision: we do not ask Ledgerwise to shorten or restart the observation window. Documented exceptions are normal in a first Type II; a restarted window would delay the report past the Series B close.

Decision: the SOC 2 status letter Northfield requested will list these three gaps with their status. No polish.

Open question: Ledgerwise may ask whether investing (live since Sep 8) is in scope for this Type II. Hana and I think yes for the backend (`brokerd`), since it's in production during the window.

## Actions

- [ ] Sam: complete Q3 access review by 2026-10-10
- [ ] Sam: MDM at 100% by 2026-10-17
- [ ] Sam: Alloy and Customer.io vendor risk assessments by 2026-10-24
- [ ] Sam: confirm investing scope with Ledgerwise by 2026-10-16
- [ ] Maya: send the SOC 2 status letter to Northfield with the data room by 2026-10-12
